name: Endogenous Cushing Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for Cushing Syndrome

criteria.description: Elevated 24-hour urinary free cortisol above the upper limit of normal on at least two measurements
Failure to suppress serum cortisol after low-dose dexamethasone suppression test
Elevated midnight serum or salivary cortisol levels
Presence of characteristic clinical features consistent with hypercortisolism

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: At least two abnormal biochemical tests confirming hypercortisolism plus compatible clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of exogenous glucocorticoid use and differentiation from pseudo-Cushing states.

pathognomonic.notes: Wide, violaceous striae on the abdomen and flanks
Predominantly affects hip and shoulder girdle muscles
searchTerms: weakness in upper arm and thigh muscles

pathognomonic.notes: Reddening of the face due to increased blood flow

common.notes: Fat accumulation in the trunk with thin limbs
Elevated blood pressure common in hypercortisolism
Excessive terminal hair growth in androgen-dependent areas
Fragile skin leading to spontaneous bruising

occasional.symptomName: Impaired glucose tolerance or diabetes mellitus
occasional.notes: Hyperglycemia due to cortisol-induced insulin resistance
Reduced bone mineral density increasing fracture risk

rare.notes: Increased risk of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism
Low serum potassium due to mineralocorticoid effects of cortisol
Rarely increased intracranial pressure may cause optic disc swelling

laboratory: Elevated midnight serum or salivary cortisol
Failure to suppress cortisol after low-dose dexamethasone
imaging: Pituitary MRI to identify adenoma in Cushing disease
Adrenal CT or MRI to detect adrenal adenoma or carcinoma
Inferior petrosal sinus sampling for ACTH source localization
genetic: Rare mutations in genes such as PRKAR1A (Carney complex)
Genetic syndromes associated with adrenal tumors (e.g., MEN1)
other: Bone densitometry showing osteopenia or osteoporosis

distinguishingFeatures: Associated with alcoholism, depression, or severe obesity
Reversible hypercortisolism without true Cushing syndrome
Normalization of cortisol after treatment of underlying condition

redFlags: Rapid onset of proximal muscle weakness
Hypokalemia with hypertension suggesting ectopic ACTH secretion
references: Nieman LK, et al. The diagnosis of Cushing's syndrome: an Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2008.
Newell-Price J, et al. Cushing's syndrome. Lancet. 2006.
Lacroix A, et al. Cushing's syndrome. Lancet. 2015.
